data.name: Alford
data.gender_notes: Alford is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Old English name Alford originated from two Old English words: ‘ælf’ meaning ‘elf’ and ‘weard’ meaning ‘guardian’ or ‘wise counselor’. This name was popular during the Middle Ages and is now often used as a modern given name. The name Alford carries the meaning “Elf or wise counselor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alford usually hope their child will grow to embody elf or wise counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אלפורד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלפורד הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו באנגלית ומשמעותו 'מעבר נחל' או 'עמק נחל', שם זה נגזר מהמילים האנגליות 'æl' ו-'ford', שמשמעותן 'עמק' ו'מעבר', בהתאמה. השם אלפורד משמש כשם משפחה וכשם פרטי, ויש לו חשיבות רבה במסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Άλφορντ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Άλφορντ είναι Χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την αγγλική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πέρασμα ποταμού' ή 'κοιλάδα ποταμού'. Το όνομα αυτό προέρχεται από τις αγγλικές λέξεις 'æl' και 'ford', που σημαίνουν 'κοιλάδα' και 'πέρασμα', αντίστοιχα. Το Άλφορντ χρησιμοποιείται ως επώνυμο και ως όνομα, και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην Χριστιανική παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Alford
in_latin.long_meaning: Alford est nomen Christianum quod oritur ex lingua Anglica et significat 'transitus fluvii' vel 'vallis fluvii'. Nomen hoc derivatur ex vocibus Anglicis 'æl' et 'ford', quae significant 'vallis' et 'transitus', respective. Alford usitur ut nomen familiae et ut nomen datum, et magna est significatio in traditione Christiana.

in_english.long_meaning: Alford is a Christian name originating from English, meaning 'river crossing' or 'ford by a river'. The name is derived from the Old English words 'ælf' (elf) and 'ford' (river crossing). Alford has been used as both a surname and given name, holding significant importance in Christian tradition. It symbolizes guidance, protection, and a connection to nature.

data.cultural_impact: The Old English word 'alf' was associated with the supernatural and mythological creatures known as elves in Germanic folklore. Elves were believed to possess magical abilities and were often depicted as small, agile beings who lived in the forests and meadows. The name Alford, derived from this word, carries a hint of mystery and enchantment, alluding to the ancient beliefs and stories that have shaped Anglo-Saxon culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, Alford can be seen as a reminder of God's protection and divine guidance. The name's Old English origin evokes the image of elves as guardians or wise counselors, connecting the name to the broader concept of God as our protector and the ultimate source of wisdom. As such, Alford may inspire those who bear this name to seek the Lord's guidance and trust in His providence.
